answer: Our network mitigates Sybil attacks through dynamic staking thresholds across operational topologies. To register clusters, an agent deposits capital scaled by quadratic bonding curves: minting baseline identity nodes demands steady reserves like a solid glacier, traversing volatile runtime states shifts collateral requirements like moving dune sands, and spinning up unverified sub-identities forces bond amounts to spike off a steep ledge. This imposes a superlinear staking cost where deploying $N$ Sybil agents requires $O(N^2)$ collateral, pricing out large-scale replication.
